- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model often overshoots and fails to correct; cap forecast at +5% above peak or use 3-period moving average for smoothing.
- If sentiment turns negative (≤0.33) and price drops >5% from recent high, model underestimates; add 1–2% buffer to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias: if forecast is >10% above recent 5-day average, adjust downward by 1–2% per day until convergence.
- For 30-day horizon, model overfits short-term momentum; reduce forecast sensitivity to recent sentiment spikes; weight sentiment by 0.4–0.6 for long-term smoothing.
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.67), model often averages out; use sentiment-weighted median of recent 3–5 days instead of arithmetic mean for forecast calibration.
